findings.motion: SB 1174 Senate Third Reading, Assembly Floor
findings.note: SB 1174 bars local governments from requiring ID to vote at polling places. He voted no on the Assembly floor (57 yes, 16 no, 6 not voting, passed).

AB 1116 (Elections: voter registration) lets a person without a California driver's license or state ID register online by giving the last four digits of their Social Security number, with the Secretary of State checking identity from that number, name and birth date. He voted no on Assembly third reading (60 yes, 18 no, 1 not voting, passed).
subjects: online voter registration without state ID

findings.passage: “Recent elections have shown just how critical it is to get results out quickly and accurately,” said Assemblymember Alanis. “AB 16 is a practical proposal that empowers election officials to start processing ballots earlier, freeing up resources and getting more of the results reported more quickly. This will help restore trust in the election process.”
findings.note: Press release from his office on his AB 16, which lets elections officials start processing mail ballots earlier. It is about speed of results and trust in elections, not ID or citizenship. Saved as related election-administration material. Page copy is from the Internet Archive because his site blocks direct fetches.
